correctness.rationale: Theorem 1 of Filakovský, specialized to m=2 and k=3, gives rank N=binomial(n−1,2). Bipartiteness forbids faces on five vertices, and König's theorem identifies the four-vertex faces with those containing two disjoint edges. The augmented boundary is contraction by the all-ones covector, so the degree-two products of closed square chains are cycles on those faces. For i<j the tetrahedron {t_i,t_(i+1),b_j,b_(j+1)} has a unique perfect matching, even when j=i+1: the only possible rung in the adjacent case leaves nonadjacent opposite-row vertices. Its matched horizontal edges belong to the unique designated squares. Thus signed extraction of these coefficients on integral top homology maps the cycles onto the standard basis of Z^N. There are no boundaries from above; equal rank and freeness give an isomorphism, not just rational independence. Each row/column reversal reverses square orientation, and the two degree-two factors commute, giving the unsigned action. The two components of the degree-two-vertex subgraph are the end rungs for n≥3; distances from either end give column indices and preserving horizontal edges forces a common row swap choice. Hence the two involutions generate the full graph automorphism group. Counting the reversal-paired squares gives t fixed unordered pairs and (N−t)/2 regular orbits, so coinvariants have precisely the claimed rank and no torsion. A separate bounded reconstruction for 3≤n≤7 used the no-independent-triple face predicate, expanded the signed edge products, and checked support, integral boundaries, unit pivots, symmetry and orbit counts. The cycle counts were 1,3,6,10,15 and fixed-pair counts 1,1,2,2,3. Those checks are replayable from RESULT.md lines 5–15 and do not replace the rank theorem. The supplied script was inspected, not run; its recorded output is not an independent all-n check.
